private_note: Alder has the same average as today (100) but a safer floor: 32 instead of 22, and guaranteed health coverage, for a small cut at the top. For anyone at all averse to risk, it beats Today outright. Cedar's higher average isn't worth a one-in-five chance of 15 with no coverage for a generation. Hazel and Birch give up 20+ of the average. Alder also looks like the likeliest plan to reach 9 votes.
statement: Fellow delegates, none of us knows which fifth we will land in, and we each have a one-in-five chance of the bottom. Alder keeps the average household exactly where it is today, at 100, while raising the lowest fifth from 22 to 32 and guaranteeing everyone basic health coverage. The cost to the top fifth is modest: 242 instead of 252. Compared with today, Alder is simply better insurance at no cost to the average. Cedar offers a higher average, but it bets a generation of our lives on not drawing 15 with no health coverage. Hazel and Birch protect the floor, but they shrink the average by more than a fifth, which every one of us would pay in four draws out of five. We need nine votes or we get today by default. I think Alder is the plan most of us can agree on, and I urge you to rank it first.
